clue.text: Second British auto company backed unknown form of government

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second

indicators.note: backed means the words for the auto company are read from the back

parts.note: a car company, written as CAR CO
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A business-page note about a British carmaker's backing, oddly tied to an unknown system of rule.
explanation.definitionFit: Mobocracy is rule by the mob, the crowd holding political power.

clue.text: 100 head of Jerseys in herd — giver of a modest income

indicators.note: in means the preceding pieces go inside the herd

parts.note: a mob is a crowd or herd
C is the Roman numeral for 100

indicators.note: head of means the first letter of Jerseys

explanation.surface: A dairy farmer's hundred Jersey cows in a herd yield a modest living.
explanation.walkthrough: A McJob is a low-paid, dead-end job, named after McDonald's.
explanation.definitionFit: A low-paid service job provides only a small wage.

clue.text: Biafran souk constructed somewhere in West Africa

indicators.note: constructed means these letters are built into a new order

explanation.surface: A market built in Biafra, somewhere in West Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: This landlocked nation, formerly Upper Volta, lies in West Africa.

clue.text: Oddly crafty Liberal US president similar to Garfield, perhaps

indicators.note: oddly means take the odd-numbered letters of crafty

parts.note: Ike was the nickname of President Eisenhower

explanation.surface: A wily Liberal compares himself with US President Garfield.
explanation.walkthrough: Garfield seems to be the assassinated president, but is the cartoon cat.
explanation.definitionFit: Garfield the comic-strip cat is the example; resembling him means feline.

clue.text: Scoffed about established male art lover?

indicators.note: about means the eating word goes round the others

parts.note: to scoff is to eat greedily, so scoffed means ate
he is a male pronoun

explanation.surface: A man of standing sneered at by those around him for loving art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scoffed' seems to mean mocked but means ate.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone devoted to beauty and the arts is an example of an art lover.

clue.text: Cowardly to express sudden pain?

definitions.meaning: lacking courage, a sense of the colour word
read as two words, a shout of 'ow!'

explanation.surface: Is crying out when hurt a coward's act?
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking bravery is the slang sense of the colour; split, it is a shout plus a cry of hurt.

clue.text: Obscure book — and what might sell it

parts.note: to obscure something is to blur it

explanation.surface: An unknown book and the cover copy that might help it sell.
explanation.definitionFit: A publisher's promotional paragraph on a cover is written to tempt buyers into a purchase.

clue.text: Branch opened up by men in part of London

indicators.note: opened up by means the branch is split to take in the next piece

parts.note: a bough is a tree branch
OR (other ranks) is the military abbreviation for men

explanation.surface: A branch office opened by staff in London.
explanation.walkthrough: London is divided into 32 boroughs, local government areas.
explanation.definitionFit: A borough is an administrative district, and London is divided into many of them.

clue.text: Benefit of American English

explanation.surface: The advantages of American English.
explanation.definitionFit: Use as a noun means advantage or value, as in 'of no use'.

clue.text: Savagery's the thing in part of North Africa

indicators.note: in means the thing goes inside the region

parts.note: Barbary is the old name for the coastal region of North Africa
it is the pronoun for a thing

explanation.surface: Cruelty is the issue in a corner of North Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbarity is brutal cruelty, an exact synonym of savage behaviour.

clue.text: Hebridean isle has little time for magistrate

parts.note: Jura is an island of the Inner Hebrides, off western Scotland
T is the short form of time

explanation.surface: An island dweller with no time for the local justice.
explanation.definitionFit: A jurat is a municipal officer or lay judge, notably in the Channel Islands, acting much like a magistrate.

clue.text: Royals are working the whole calendar

indicators.note: working means these letters are being worked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: The royal family busy at engagements every day of the year.
explanation.definitionFit: The time Earth takes to circle the Sun is the span a full calendar covers.

clue.text: Caribou bit him — son left writhing in part of Canada

indicators.note: writhing means twisting about, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A caribou bites a man and his son is left in agony somewhere in Canada.
explanation.walkthrough: 'writhing' shuffles CARIBOUBITHIM plus S and L.
explanation.definitionFit: This is Canada's westernmost province, on the Pacific coast.

clue.text: Kept too bad a cooked snack

indicators.note: cooked means these letters are messed with, rearranged

explanation.surface: A dish kept too long, badly cooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' looks like the anagram signal but is part of the fodder; 'cooked' rearranges KEPTTOOBADA.
explanation.definitionFit: A jacket spud with filling is a light meal, an example of something to eat between meals.

clue.text: What may protect legs in ballet leap without a catcher

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the leap goes around the rest

parts.note: a jeté is a ballet leap from one foot to the other
a net catches fish or butterflies

explanation.surface: A dancer leaps without anyone there to catch them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not lacking. Jeanette is a twilled cotton fabric, used for trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: A cotton cloth made into trousers would cover and shield the wearer's lower limbs.

clue.text: What may fumigate small parasite after girl's sulphur

indicators.note: after means the small parasite follows the girl's sulphur

parts.note: Jo's, the possessive of the girl's name Jo
S is the chemical symbol for sulphur
a tick is a blood-sucking parasite

explanation.surface: A parasite treated with sulphur after a girl gets it.
explanation.definitionFit: An incense stick burnt in a temple fills a room with fragrant smoke, a kind of fumigation.

clue.text: Devotion to god and king — habit's developed about that

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go around the next piece
developed means the letters of habit change into a new form

explanation.surface: A monk's devotion to god and king grows around his habit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developed' rearranges HABIT; 'about' puts that around K.
explanation.definitionFit: Bhakti is the Hindu path of loving worship of a chosen deity.

clue.text: Drink to be declined for first two persons, not drinking round

parts.words: to be declined for first two persons
parts.note: the verb to be in the first and second persons: I am, you are
TT, teetotal
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A drink refused by two people who are not drinking a round.
explanation.definitionFit: Amaretto is an Italian almond liqueur.

clue.text: Second cloth for baby, quick

parts.note: a nappy is the British word for a diaper

explanation.surface: A second baby's diaper needed, and fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Snappy can mean brisk or fast, as in 'make it snappy'.

clue.text: What comes of books breaking spine?

indicators.note: breaking means the books burst into the middle of spine

parts.note: spine in the sense of courage, pluck
OT, the Old Testament, is a set of books

explanation.surface: A library worry: what happens when book spines crack?
explanation.walkthrough: 'spine' is courage, not a book's back.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking whatever happens to be available is accepting chance's offering.

clue.text: Fast uncovered members' odd ways

indicators.note: uncovered means each of the three words loses its outer letters, its covering

explanation.surface: Club members' strange habits laid bare quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast' is the noun, a period of fasting, not speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Ember days are set days of prayer and fasting in the Western church calendar.

clue.text: Character of German city church

parts.note: Essen is a city in the Ruhr
CE, the Church of England

explanation.surface: The character of a German city's church.
explanation.definitionFit: The essential nature or core quality of something is its character.

clue.text: Wife leans over car

parts.note: a ship heels when it leans over

explanation.surface: A wife leaning over a car.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a car or a means of transport, as in 'got some new wheels'.

clue.text: Severe corrective instruments keeping tots from wine

indicators.note: keeping here means holding apart, as one piece sits between two others
from completes keeping X from Y, showing the separated pieces either side

parts.note: tots are small drinks of spirits, shorts in British slang
harps are musical instruments
hock is a German white wine

explanation.surface: Instruments of punishment that stop children getting to the wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping ... from' means separating: the instruments stand between the tots and the wine. The phrase named a 1980s British policy of brief harsh detention for young offenders.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief harsh punishment meant to deter, a deliberately stern correction.

clue.text: Bent German sausage? Not half

indicators.note: not half means only the front half of the sausage name is kept

parts.note: knackwurst is a short thick German sausage

explanation.surface: Is a curved German sausage only half there?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bent' is a noun, a natural talent, not curved.
explanation.definitionFit: A natural aptitude or flair for something is a bent.

clue.text: Naughty child, bad-mannered not heartlessly reckless

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child
rude means bad-mannered

indicators.note: heartlessly means the word not loses its middle letter

explanation.surface: A rude child, not quite heartless, behaving rashly.
explanation.definitionFit: Imprudent means unwise or rash, acting without care.

clue.text: Odd characters in party are very intrusive

indicators.note: odd characters in means the first, third and fifth letters of party

explanation.surface: Odd people at a party are nosy.
explanation.definitionFit: To poke into others' business is to be nosy and meddling.

clue.text: Antelope US university nearly introduced to North America

indicators.note: introduced to means put inside the following piece
nearly means the university name stops one letter short

parts.note: Yale is an Ivy League university

explanation.surface: An African antelope almost brought to an American campus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' drops the university's last letter; 'introduced to' places the rest inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The nyala is a spiral-horned southern African antelope.

clue.text: Vessel taking girl a kilometre

parts.note: Kay is a girl's name
K is short for kilometre

explanation.surface: A boat takes a girl a kilometre downstream.
explanation.definitionFit: A kayak is a small boat, a vessel paddled by one person.

clue.text: Bird concealing fresh egg in wall?

indicators.note: concealing means the bird wraps round what follows

parts.note: a stork is a wading bird
fresh means new
an egg is O-shaped

explanation.surface: A bird hides a newly laid egg in a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: A wall built of masonry is an example of construction in cut stone.
